newsitem.title: USA: Estee Lauder net sales hurt by strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: Estee Lauder net sales hurt by strong dollar.

text.p: Estee Lauder Cos Inc said on Tuesday that its net sales for the most recent quarter were up four percent but would have risen seven percent except for the impact of the strong dollar.

Still, Estee Lauder's net income per share of $0.27 exceeded by $0.02 analysts' consensus estimate for its third quarter ending March 31. The company had net income of $0.19 per share for the same period the year before.

Estee Lauder said its Asia/Pacific net sales grew seven percent on a local-currency basis, with increases in every market except Hong Kong. But due to foreign currency translation, especially the dollar's strength against the Japanese yen, net sales in the region were down one percent.
In Europe, the Middle East and Africa, net sales were up nine percent excluding the currency exchange impact, but only up two percent after factoring in the strong dollar.
In the Americas, sales were up six percent, which the company attributed in part to new product launches across all categories.
Estee Lauder shares were trading up 5/8 to 44-1/2 on Tuesday at mid-morning.
